{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The lighthouse at Corrin Point had been automated the summer Tobias Fenn turned nineteen, and for a while nobody noticed that he kept climbing the stairs anyway.

His grandfather had been the last keeper. The old man had taught Tobias to read the water the way other people read handwriting: the oily flatness that meant fog was gathering offshore, the green light under a breaking wave that promised a shifting bar, the way the gulls went inland an hour before a squall.

The maritime authority now ran the lamp on a timer and monitored the channel from a control room ninety miles south. It did this competently. Tobias did not distrust the timer so much as he distrusted the idea that a coast could be watched from a place where it could not be heard.

So he went up most evenings, wiped the salt from the glass, and logged what he saw in a ledger he showed to no one.

In October a storm took down the relay mast. The control room, blind to one point among dozens, marked the channel clear from the last reading. A fishing boat radioed for a heading. Tobias, from the sound of the swell against the rocks and the way the buoy had stopped ringing, knew the bar had moved.

He lit the old oil lamp by hand and swung it twice, the way his grandfather had shown him. The boat turned. It came in on the far side of the bar, scraping but afloat.

The inquiry noted an unauthorized signal of undetermined origin.

Tobias bought a new ledger."}
